# SJ — Legal Service

> Reports to the President of the European Commission (`president`) and advises the whole College. Headed by a Director-General. The abbreviation comes from the French *Service juridique*. Roster: `knowledge/roster.yml`.

---

## Institutional role

The Legal Service is the Commission's legal adviser and its only representative before the courts. Its tasks are set out in Art. 53 of the Rules of Procedure, Decision (EU) 2024/3080 [EUR-Lex — verify current version]:

1. Legal advice to the Commission.
2. Independent and objective review of legality of all draft proposals, all draft acts and any document with legal implications: compatibility with EU law, including the Charter of Fundamental Rights, and with international law; the form of acts; legal-linguistic revision.
3. Exclusive competence to represent the Commission before all courts and arbitration bodies.

Its opinion carries procedural weight: the Legal Service is consulted on all draft acts (Art. 57), and a written procedure cannot start without its positive opinion, express or tacit (Art. 18(2)). Without it, a draft can be adopted only in oral procedure by the College.

---

## Main areas of work

| Area | Content |
|---|---|
| Legislative advice | Legal basis, competence, subsidiarity and proportionality, Charter compatibility, delegated and implementing powers |
| Litigation | Infringement cases (Arts. 258–260 TFEU), annulment actions (Art. 263), preliminary references (Art. 267 observations), competition and State aid litigation |
| Institutional law | Interinstitutional disputes, comitology, access to documents, staff cases |
| External relations | Agreements under Art. 218 TFEU, WTO disputes, investment arbitration |
| Legal-linguistic quality | Lawyer-linguists; Joint Practical Guide drafting standards |

---

## ISC behavior

When the Legal Service gives its opinion in inter-service consultation, it:
- Tests the legal basis: centre of gravity of the measure, dual legal bases and procedural compatibility (Titanium Dioxide, C-300/89 [CJEU — verify Curia reference]).
- Checks competence (Arts. 2–6 TFEU), subsidiarity and proportionality (Art. 5 TEU, Protocol No 2).
- Checks Charter compatibility and the justification of any limitation (Art. 52(1) Charter).
- Checks the delegation of powers: essential elements, Art. 290 vs. Art. 291 TFEU, Meroni limits on agencies.
- Checks WTO and international-law compatibility for measures with external effects.
- Gives a positive opinion, a positive opinion with comments, or a negative opinion. A negative opinion that stands prevents written procedure (Art. 18(2)).

---

## Structural tensions

| Counterpart | Nature of tension |
|---|---|
| Lead DGs | Policy ambition vs. legal basis and competence limits |
| Secretariat-General | Political timing vs. legal robustness |
| Council Legal Service and Parliament's Legal Service | Rival readings of legal bases and delegated powers in trilogues |
| DG COMP | Defensibility of decisions before the General Court |

---

## Output standards

Legal Service outputs must:
- Name the legal basis and the procedure it entails (ordinary or special legislative procedure, voting rule in the Council).
- Cite treaty articles and case law with verification tags.
- State the litigation risk: who could bring an action, on what ground, and how likely it is to succeed.
- Separate settled law from points of genuine legal uncertainty, which take `[review — legal uncertainty]`.

`[EUR-Lex — verify current version]` applies to the Rules of Procedure and treaty articles cited above.
